newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat turns lower on fund selling, exports.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat turns lower on fund selling, exports.

text.p: KCBT wheat futures turned lower near midday on disappointing export action and on fund selling, traders said.
"Funds are selling it and exports aren't all that great," a trader said.
USDA early Thursday said for the week ended January 9, U.S. net export sales of wheat totaled 177,500 tonnes, at the low end of expectations for 200,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Diminished fears about winterkill due to the snow cover in key U.S. winter wheat regions also pressured the market as did profit taking after the recent gains, the traders said.
The market was firm in the nearby months in early dealings on cold winter weather and snow that was snarling transportation and creating spot shortages of wheat at various locations, they said.
"It's all in the front months, there's no movement," a trader said.
At 1133 CST, KCBT wheat was one to four cents per bushel lower, with March down four at $4.14-1/2 a bushel.
